the same-seed off burst EVEN with turbulence armed (the decoupling crux), but the rotation sequence changes
-> its own committed hash (SPINRATE_HASH 1105261140), deterministic under a fixed seed + fixed dt. Composes
with `align`: the tumble scale runs FIRST, then align lerps toward the velocity heading.

No new probe. Reuses the v1.15.0 `rotateHash` / `lastRotate` pair -- the FIRST orientation feature to ship
without a harness change. The `lastRotate` witness proves the knob scales the RATE: a pumped spinRate:0 piece
freezes at its birth tilt (does not advance), while spinRate:1 keeps turning.

Internal + fail closed. Two per-particle pool columns: `spin0` (the random birth pivot, written right after
the spin seed in spawn()) and `spinRate` (the multiplier, assigned beside `align`); 8 B/particle. spawn()
always writes both, so the TypedArray zero-init is never relied on (a zero spinRate means "frozen"). The
render scale is guarded (`spin0 + (spin - spin0) * rate`, paid ONLY for scaled pieces, BEFORE the align
blend; a read + compare when off) -- zero allocation, no physics change. `rot` is a bounded seeded angle
times a finite multiplier, hence finite for any finite spinRate. Inert under reduced motion (the static fan
has no accumulated tumble to scale). Unit suite 173 -> 182.

## v1.15.0 -- align / velocity-aligned orientation

The FIRST feature on a new RENDER-ORIENTATION axis. For fourteen releases a piece's rotation was only ever
RANDOM tumble (a seeded `spin` + a `flutter` X-scale wobble); this opens WHICH WAY it faces. An opt-in
`align` (a 0..1 blend) rotates each piece BROADSIDE to its LIVE velocity (`atan2(vy,vx)+PI/2`, so the flat
face meets the airflow like a falling leaf), re-banking every frame as gravity/wind/vortex bend the path --
e.g. c.burst({ align: 1, gravity: 200, wind: 300, spread: 0.4 }). Unlike burst-only `stagger`, both burst
AND spray honor it (a render property of any moving piece).

Locked decisions. (1) Live velocity heading over a launch-heading frozen at spawn: the heading is
recomputed from the current (vx,vy) each frame, so an aligned piece continuously re-orients as forces curve
its trajectory (one atan2 per aligned piece per frame, on the render path only). (2) Broadside over edge-on:
`rotate(heading + HALF_PI)` sits the long axis perpendicular to travel so the flat face meets the airflow
(a leaf), not the long axis parallel (a card knifing forward). (3) A 0..1 shortest-arc blend: lerp from the
random `spin` toward the heading along the short way round the circle, so a spin near a full turn never
unwinds the long way; draws no rng.

The byte-identical-POSITION-stream crux. `align` changes ONLY the argument to `ctx.rotate`; it never moves
`ctx.translate`. The position fingerprint folds only translate (rotation/scale are hash-neutral -- which is
why `flutter` has always been), so an aligned burst draws the IDENTICAL translate sequence as a same-seed
plain burst; only the rotation differs. OFF (`align 0`) -> the guard is false -> the raw `spin` is emitted,
position AND rotation byte-identical to every prior release (COMMITTED_HASH 1569828004 and all prior hashes
preserved). ON -> the position hash is STILL identical to the same-seed off burst (a pure orientation
overlay, the analog of lifeColors on the color axis), but the rotation sequence changes -> its own committed
hash (ALIGN_HASH 1909618495), deterministic under a fixed seed + fixed dt.

A new probe WAS needed. Rotation is invisible to the position hash, so a bare fingerprint cannot see it. The
mock canvas's rotate() (a no-op until now) gained a `rotateHash` that folds the quantized angle (kept out of
the position hash, like strokeHash/colorHash/translates), plus a `lastRotate` DIRECTION accessor -- the
non-vacuous witness that the rotation TRACKS the velocity heading (a rightward-blown piece stands broadside
~HALF_PI), not merely "some different number".

Internal + fail closed. One per-particle pool column `align` (Float32, blend 0..1; 4 B/particle), assigned
from config in spawn() like `flut`/`sway`. The render-rotation blend is guarded (one atan2 + a shortest-arc
wrap + a lerp, paid ONLY for aligned pieces; a read + compare when off) -- zero allocation, no physics
change. `clamp01` coerces non-finite/negative -> 0 and caps >1 at 1; atan2 is total (atan2(0,0)===0 for a
settled piece), so the rotation is finite for any finite velocity. Inert under reduced motion (the static
fan has no velocity to orient to). Unit suite 165 -> 173.

## v1.14.0 -- stagger / staggered emission

The FIRST feature on a new EMISSION-TIMING axis. v1.13 opened emission GEOMETRY (where a piece is born);
this opens WHEN. A burst has always spawned its whole `count` at frame 0; an opt-in `stagger` (a
duration in ms) spreads the births evenly across that window, so a burst cascades / ripples in instead
of appearing at once -- e.g. c.burst({ count: 120, stagger: 400 }). It is the BURST-only analog of a
spray's `duration` (a spray already emits over time); `spray()` ignores it.

Locked decisions. (1) Birth-delay gate over a deferred spray-style drip: all `count` pieces spawn at
CALL TIME (so the rng sequence is byte-identical to a synchronous burst), each stamped with a per-piece
`delay`; an unborn piece is frozen + invisible until its delay elapses, then lives its FULL life from
birth. Reuses the settle-freeze pattern + the existing ensureRunning path; no retained emitter closure.
(2) Duration window in ms over a per-particle step: the `count` is spread evenly across the window
(piece i wakes at stagger*i/count), so the window is stable as count changes; emission order is linear
and draws no rng.

The byte-identical rng-sequence crux. A staggered burst draws the IDENTICAL rng sequence as a
synchronous burst of the same seed + count; ONLY birth timing differs. All pieces spawn in the existing
loop (same draws, same order), and `delay = staggerSec * i / count` is a function of the loop INDEX
only (no rng); update() draws no rng, so freezing a piece changes nothing about the stream. So OFF
(delay all 0) is byte-identical -- COMMITTED_HASH (1569828004) and every prior physics/trail/color/emit
hash preserved; ON earns its own committed hash (STAGGER_HASH 3414676538) purely from birth timing
(same per-piece angle/speed/spin, spread across frames), deterministic under a fixed seed + fixed dt.

A new probe WAS needed. Unborn pieces count as alive (so the loop stays registered), so `.count` cannot
show the timing. The mock canvas gained a `translates` counter (one per DRAWN piece per frame, kept out
of the position hash): a staggered burst draws far fewer pieces in the early frames, converging to all
`count` per frame once the window elapses -- the non-vacuous witness that births are delayed.

Internal + fail closed. One per-particle pool column `delay` (Float32, 4 B/particle), reset to 0 in
spawn() (fail-closed pool-reuse guard, like `landed`); spawn() now RETURNS its slot so the burst loop
can stamp the delay, and the write runs only when armed. The birth gate is one Float32 read + compare
per alive piece per frame (mirrors the life <= 0 / !landed guards); an unborn piece skips physics +
life-countdown + trail + render but counts as alive. Fail closed: NaN / negative / Infinity /
non-numeric coerce to 0 (synchronous); the delay is a time offset of the finite spawn origin, so no
non-finite draw can result. Burst-only; inert under reduced motion; ~0 B/frame (a store at spawn + a
read/compare/frame). See decision 0015. No runtime dep change. Unit suite 157 -> 165.

## v1.13.0 -- emit / emitter shapes

The FIRST feature on a new EMISSION-GEOMETRY axis. Every chapter changed how a particle MOVES (forces),
ENDS (settle), or is DRAWN (trails, color); this changes WHERE it is BORN. Two knobs: `emit`
('line' | 'ring' | 'box') + `emitSize` (one scalar). Instead of the single point (x, y), a burst
distributes its spawn origin over a shape -- a horizontal `line` curtain (rain/snow), a `ring` firework
shell, or a `box` area -- e.g. c.burst({ emit: 'ring', emitSize: 140, speed: 6 }).

Locked decisions. (1) A single `emitSize` scalar sizes every shape (line half-length / ring radius / box
square half-extent) -- house style over an `emit` object (angled lines / rectangular boxes deferred).
(2) Ring = radial shell: for `emit:'ring'` ONLY, each piece's velocity points radially OUTWARD from the
centre (speed = expansion rate, spread = angular fuzz), reusing the already-drawn spread jitter; line/box
leave velocity to angle/spread and move only the origin.

The conditional spawn-rng contract (the crux). `emit` is the FIRST feature to add a conditional spawn-time
rng draw. The emitter branch sits in the spawn loop AFTER the speed draw and BEFORE spawn(). `EMIT_OFF`
(the default) inserts NOTHING -- the loop draws the identical angle then speed then calls the point
spawn() -- so the seeded stream and EVERY committed position fingerprint (1569828004, and all prior
physics/trail/color hashes) are byte-identical to a point burst. Per-shape draw counts differ: line/ring
draw 1 (the parametric position), box draws 2 (independent x/y). Because the counts differ, each shape
earns its OWN committed hash -- line 2558715937, ring 2441425203, box 2748626140 -- all distinct from the
point spawn and each other; within a shape the count is fixed, so it replays identically under a seed.

No probe needed. Unlike trails/lifeColors (which draw in world space or move only fillStyle -- invisible
to the position hash, needing strokeHash/colorHash), `emit` MOVES the spawn origin, and the mock canvas
already folds translate(x,y) into the position hash, so the existing fingerprint observes it directly.

Internal + fail closed. Module consts EMIT_OFF/LINE/RING/BOX + an EMIT_ID string->int Map, resolved once
per burst/spray (emitId/emitR locals), so the spawn loop branches on an int, not a string. spawn()'s
signature is UNCHANGED -- the emitter computes the origin (and, for ring, the velocity) in the caller.
An unknown/non-string shape or a non-positive/non-finite emitSize collapses to EMIT_OFF (a point spawn);
the origin is an offset of the finite burst centre, so no non-finite draw position can result. Inert
under reduced motion (the static fan has no rng origin); the hot render path is untouched (emit only
moves the origin). Unit suite 149 -> 157; every prior position/trail/color fingerprint preserved when
off; ~0 B/frame at spawn (a few multiplies on stack locals, the shape-id an int).

## v1.12.0 -- color / lifeColors

The second RENDER feature (after trails). Every chapter changed how a particle MOVES (forces), ENDS
(settle), or is SHAPED; this changes how it is COLORED over time. One knob: `lifeColors` -- an ordered
list of >= 2 OKLCH stops (birth-color first). The BODY of each piece sweeps the ramp as it ages --
sparks cooling white -> orange -> red, embers dimming -- e.g.
c.burst({ lifeColors: [{l:.98,c:.02,h:90}, {l:.72,c:.22,h:60}, {l:.40,c:.15,h:30}] }).

Law -- baked LUT, indexed by life. The color model already pre-parsed OKLCH -> CSS strings ONCE per
burst (never toCssOklch per frame). lifeColors keeps that: `buildLifeRamp` bakes the stops ONCE into a
fixed-resolution LUT of CSS strings via lite-color's bakeCssGradient (RAMP_N = 32 steps), and the
render loop indexes it by the piece's life fraction (`step = clamp(floor((1 - life/maxL) * (RAMP_N-1)))`,
birth = stop 0, death = last) -- a pure array read, zero per-frame color math, zero allocation.

Pure color overlay. The ONLY hot-path change is which string fillStyle gets. `colors[i]` is STILL
picked per particle (one rng.pick, unchanged), so the spawn rng sequence -- and thus EVERY committed
position fingerprint -- is byte-identical: a lifeColors burst reproduces the same-seed plain burst's
position hash exactly (the render-axis analog of trails). The palette `colors` stays the flat TRAIL
color (locked decision) and the body color when off; all pieces share one ramp, so variety comes from
their different life phases. Since color never enters the position hash, the test canvas gained a
`colorHash` probe (folds fillStyle at each body paint, kept out of the position hash) -- a lifeColors
burst's colorHash differs (COLOR_HASH 2406267552) while its position hash is unchanged.

Fail closed. `buildLifeRamp` returns null (=> the body paints the flat colors[i], not the default
rainbow) for a non-array, < 2 stops, or any non-finite / unparseable stop; parseOklch THROWS on a bad
string, so the whole bake is wrapped in try/catch. spawn() always (re)assigns colorRamp[i] (the shared
LUT or null), so a recycled slot never inherits a prior burst's ramp. No reduced-motion effect (the
static render does no life integration, so it paints the flat color). Unit suite 141 -> 149; every
prior position/trail fingerprint preserved; ~0 B/frame (LUT baked once, hot path an array read).

## v1.11.0 -- settle / pile

The first BEHAVIOUR (lifecycle) feature. Every chapter before changed how a particle MOVES (forces)
or DRAWS (trails); this changes how it ENDS. One flat-scalar knob: `settle` (rest-speed threshold,
px/s; 0 = off). A piece bounces on the `floor` (losing energy to bounce < 1 + drag) until the
rebound is too weak to lift it -- its reflected |vy| drops below `settle` -- then it FREEZES in
place and piles up instead of bouncing forever -- c.burst({ floor: 520, bounce: 0.4, settle: 60 }).

Law -- bounce-then-rest. The rest test lives INSIDE the (already opt-in) floor block: right after
the floor clamps y and reflects vy, if `settle != 0 && |vy| < settle` the piece is marked landed
(vx = vy = 0). A landed piece is frozen: the WHOLE physics span (gravity through the wall clamps) is
wrapped in `if (!landed)`, so it skips integration, collision, spin, tilt, and sway -- position AND
rotation frozen, so a pile lies still and wind/gust/sway can't nudge it. With bounce 0 a piece rests
on first contact; a higher bounce just delays the rest (drag still bleeds energy each frame), and
with no floor this branch is unreachable so nothing ever settles (fail-closed -- needs a floor).

Keeps aging, transient pile. A landed piece still counts down its life and fades in place (the life
countdown + fade + trail record + render all sit OUTSIDE the freeze wrap), then its slot recycles --
so the fixed zero-GC pool never saturates and new bursts always spawn. The alternative (freeze
immortal = a permanent pile) would saturate the pool and block spawns, so it is deliberately NOT the
default. Garbage coerces via nonneg() (NaN/negative/string -> 0 = off); a settled piece rests at a
finite floor Y, so no non-finite draw position can result.

Zero rng (a pure function of the piece's own post-bounce velocity), so a settling burst replays
identically under a fixed seed with its own committed fingerprint (SETTLE_HASH 4157000621 on a
bounce-0.5 floor rig), while the default (settle 0) leaves `landed` always 0, so the `if (!landed)`
wrap always runs and EVERY prior fingerprint is preserved (default 1569828004, floored 2679696825,
box 804161759, all forces, and the v1.9.0 trail geometry -- positions untouched). Two per-particle
pool columns (settle Float32 + landed Uint8, 5 B/particle); spawn() resets landed = 0 (a recycled
slot can never inherit a dead piece's frozen state). No hot-path alloc -- a frozen pile is pure
reads. No reduced-motion effect (the static render never integrates, so nothing lands).

The unit gate asserts default/floor/box hashes byte-identical (the freeze wrap + guard never fire
when off), opt-in/fail-closed settle == the same bouncy run, pins SETTLE_HASH (distinct from bouncy,
deterministic), and proves NON-VACUOUS effects a bare hash can't see: settle ARRESTS lateral drift
(a settled pool spreads less than a still-sliding one under wind), the pile STOPS GROWING while an
un-settled pool keeps sliding (comes to rest), pieces pile AT the floor (maxY == floor) and need a
floor to settle; plus assertFinite under settle+sway+wind+gravity in a box (contained). Torture T5
threads settle + a floor through the differential fuzz; T6 adds a fully-settled (frozen) pile lane
to the alloc gate; T1 adds settle + floor poison under the finite-position detector. See decision
0012. No runtime dep change. Unit suite 132 -> 141.
